answer: A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. Written in a clipped, no filler register, it stays short. Each submission hangs on the kernel of a task receipt, and the grove is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. By the reef of the epoch the only identities still standing are the ones whose work held up. The design leans on slash-on-divergence jury quorum, clawed back after a replayed submission, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work.
